title: From Uniform to Learned Graph Priors: Diffusion for Structure Discovery

problem.claim: Neural relational inference methods discover interaction graphs from trajectories through variational reasoning over discrete potential edges.

gap.claim: Existing methods typically use factorized, near-uniform graph priors that treat edges independently, producing diffuse and indecisive edge posteriors that limit structural-discovery reliability.

contributions.claim: Diff-prior is a diffusion-parameterized adaptive prior for calibrating latent graph distributions rather than generating graphs.
Diff-prior performs structured calibration on encoder edge posteriors during inference before structural sampling.
The method reframes prior integration as learnable denoising-style calibration for structured variables.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on standard benchmarks reportedly validated the framework and indicated improved structure-inference performance across multiple NRI-family architectures.
The authors report that Diff-prior generates more decisive edge posteriors.

narrative_sequence.summary: NRI methods infer interaction graphs from trajectories using variational reasoning over discrete potential edges.
Common factorized, near-uniform priors misalign with real-world systems and yield uncertain edge posteriors.
Diff-prior introduces diffusion-based adaptive prior calibration for latent graph distributions.
Benchmark experiments reportedly show improved inference performance and more decisive posteriors across NRI-family architectures.

source_observation.claim: Independent, near-uniform priors can produce diffuse edge posteriors when the target structure is not well modeled by factorization.

interpretation.claim: For structured latent-variable inference, learning dependencies in the prior may improve posterior decisiveness.

application.claim: Use adaptive denoising-style prior calibration before sampling when inference involves uncertain structured variables.

exception.claim: The abstract only reports results on standard benchmarks and multiple NRI-family architectures; broader applicability is unspecified.

unknowns: Benchmark datasets, metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The diffusion architecture, training objective, and calibration procedure are unspecified.
Comparative limitations, computational cost, and failure cases are unspecified.
